rationale: No panel dissent is attached to this packet. The judgment did change, so a complete assessment is returned. Three things moved. (1) VASO-C004, the anchor phenomenon, moves from unresolved to weakly_supported: the claim as written is about a felt release, and the only record on it (VASO-E014) is testimony that supports a felt event and is contradicted by nothing; the crux — whether anything objective happens — is carried by diagnosticity (low for the felt event, high for its objective correlate), not by calling an uncontradicted first-person report undecided. (2) VASO-C001 moves from well_supported to provisionally_supported: its direct ledger records are one weak proponent record (VASO-E015) with unverified statistics, a moderate qualifying record (VASO-E012) that says the reproducibility and ontological status of the discrete spot are themselves disputed, and a context record; the residual standing leans on the instrumented findings under VASO-C005 and on priors, and the reasoning says so. A well_supported grade sat awkwardly beside the ledger's own statement that the dispute reaches the observation base. (3) The incumbent assessment carried a null steelman and no per-claim treatments; both are now supplied for every featured claim, with diagnosticity graded separately from credibility so the reader can see that the best-evidenced rungs (VASO-C010, VASO-C013, VASO-C012) are the least decisive. The case verdict remains unresolved, with the synthesis now naming VASO-E020 as the record whose removal would most change the shape of the case (VASO-C020 would revert from 'examined and mismatched' to 'untested') while VASO-E016 stays the single most important undermining record. Load-bearing adds VASO-C002, since the electrically maintained nidus is the one instrumented observation that separates state from scar in the ledger. Six components replace the informal ladder. Selection is unchanged — the ledger holds fourteen claims and all fourteen are featured. Crux order adds the two research items entered since the incumbent (VASO-R008 densification-versus-latch and VASO-R009 the phentolamine retrieval), placing them directly after the keystone and latch studies because each is a cheap desk item that sharpens the keystone's discriminating prediction; the executed evidence map (VASO-R007) goes last. The article is rewritten to cite only what is in the ledger — the Piezo Nobel, the dorsal-root-ganglion capillary anatomy, and the meditation-adverse-effects literature are removed or reduced to attributed proponent argument — and now carries the arteriole record from VASO-S001 in its own section, names fascial densification as a non-vascular state-level competitor, flags the unlocated phentolamine study, presents an explicit two-directional 'what would change our mind' section, and ends with the ledger's verdict and the steelman in plain view. Both plates are retained.
article:
There is a strange gap at the center of musculoskeletal medicine. Anyone with a foam roller and twenty minutes can find [dozens of small, discrete, exquisitely tender points in their own body]{claim=VASO-C001} — most densely around the hips and shoulders, by common report more numerous with each passing decade. Roll across one and it announces itself. Yet open the research literature and you find scientists arguing about what these points are — and, in part, [about whether the “trigger point” is a real, reliably identifiable thing at all]{claim=VASO-C030}.

This case examines a chain of ideas offered to close that gap. It runs from textbook smooth-muscle physiology, through a minority hypothesis about blood and computation, to Tibetan and Indian contemplative anatomy, and it arrives at a proposal with a slogan: a knot is a *state*, not a *scar* — something the body is actively doing and could stop doing, rather than tissue that has been damaged. The lower rungs of the chain are established science. The upper rungs have never been tested. And the one experiment that would decide the central question has never been run.

## A phenomenon without a mechanism

Part of the reason the fight has run so long is structural. Medicine is organized by organ system: orthopedics owns bones, neurology owns nerves, cardiology owns the pipes. Nobody owns muscle tone — the continuous, neurally set background contraction of soft tissue. No specialty means no billing codes, no imaging protocols, no funding lines. The skeptics’ favorite line, “there is no evidence,” is partly circular: there is little evidence in part because nobody has been paid to look.

But the skeptical case deserves its full weight, and it is heavier than proponents usually grant. A systematic review of examination-reliability studies (Lucas and colleagues, 2009) concluded that manual examination for trigger points has not been shown to be reliable or valid — partly because no accepted reference standard exists for what one is — and could not be recommended as an objective diagnostic test. The most pointed peer-reviewed critique (Quintner, Bove and Cohen, 2015) argues that the construct rests on circular reasoning: the lesion has never been demonstrated, examiners disagree, and the clinical phenomena can be explained otherwise. That critique drew a rebuttal, and the exchange rather than either paper is the state of the debate. Still, the dispute is not only about mechanism. It reaches the observation base: the reproducibility and even the ontological status of the discrete palpable spot are part of the academic argument. That is why this case grades the first claim above as *provisionally* rather than *well* supported — the shared experience is vast, but the instrumented record behind “discrete” and “palpable” is thinner than it feels under the fingertip.

What survives the critique is a set of instrumented findings. Shah and colleagues (2008) sampled the fluid at active trigger points and found [it more acidic and loaded with mediators of pain and inflammation — bradykinin, substance P, CGRP]{claim=VASO-C005}; a 2021 systematic review of 33 imaging studies reports that stiffness and blood-flow measures can distinguish active and latent trigger points from healthy tissue, with reproducibility caveats attached. Two cautions travel with these. The microdialysis study had about nine volunteers and, as its own title says, the mediators were elevated at sites remote from the points as well as near them. And the imaging review’s characterization in this ledger is second-hand, taken from a critical report rather than the paper’s full text. Something is there, and it is chemically angry — but whether what is there is *local* is less settled than it sounds.

Then there is the phenomenology practitioners report, which any candidate mechanism must explain. The obstruction feels like a dull blockage rather than a sharp stretch-pain. Knots accumulate and hold flexibility hostage. And — the strange one — [pressure locates a knot, but release comes with breath: press in, exhale slowly, and something lets go within seconds]{claim=VASO-C004}. Fresh knots yield in a session; old ones take months. This case labels that report for what it is: first-person testimony from the hypothesis’s own proponent, in an essay whose text was generated by AI models at the author’s direction; consistent with widespread practitioner lore; contradicted by no one; measured by no one. It is real evidence that people *feel* a release. It is no evidence at all that anything happens in the tissue. It is the anchor phenomenon of everything that follows.

## Two experiments that catch the loop in motion

The evidence that these spots are under ongoing neural control has existed for decades, largely unread. In 1993, Hubbard and Berkoff inserted fine needle electrodes into trapezius trigger points and, simultaneously, into adjacent non-tender fibers. They recorded [sustained spontaneous electrical activity confined to a one-to-two-millimeter nidus, and none in the non-tender sites]{claim=VASO-C002}, with higher amplitude in tension-headache and fibromyalgia patients than in healthy subjects. The knot is not merely stiffer than its surroundings; it is a small island of maintained activity in muscle nominally at rest. The authors guessed that sympathetically driven muscle-spindle contractions were the source; later literature favors endplate potentials; the generator remains contested.

The follow-up, from McNulty, Gevirtz, Hubbard and Berkoff in 1994, is the remarkable one. With electrodes in place in fourteen subjects, they administered mental arithmetic. [Activity at the trigger point rose; control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet; the subjects were not tensing]{claim=VASO-C003}. A purely mental event, involving no movement, turned up the signal inside one tender point and not a centimeter away. The brain has the knot’s address. Both studies are small, old, from one lineage, and never replicated with modern instrumentation, and neither took any vascular measurement. The essay this case grew from adds two follow-ups from the same lineage — relaxation training lowering the activity, and an infusion of the alpha-blocker phentolamine quieting the site — for which no primary paper has been located in this project. Finding it is one of the research items below; until then the autonomic-maintenance argument rests on stress induction alone.

Then, in August 2026, a study in *Nature Human Behaviour* supplied the regulatory counterpart. Mizrachi, Rottem and Rozenkrantz induced identical histamine skin-prick inflammation in the same fifty-seven volunteers on different occasions, in preregistered experiments, manipulating only where attention went. [Attending to the inflamed site produced roughly 1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving wheal-and-flare responses in about ninety percent of participants across two cohorts — with no difference in skin conductance, heart rate, skin temperature or self-reported anxiety, and heart-rate variability higher under inward attention]{claim=VASO-C006}. A local anesthetic dissected two routes: a sensory one that lidocaine degraded and a top-down vagal one that survived it. What this shows is that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site without arousal. What it does not show is anything about knots, smooth muscle, or seconds: the timescale was tens of minutes and the route is vagal immune regulation, in a tissue the authors note the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate. It is an existence proof for a channel, not for the featured mechanism.

## The ratchet in the vessel walls

{plate:IMG-VASO-P02}

The body contains a second muscular system under no direct voluntary command: smooth muscle, lining the blood vessels, gut and airways, answering to autonomic state. Smooth muscle has a property skeletal muscle lacks, textbook physiology since Hai and Murphy formalized it in 1988: [the latch-bridge state, in which its molecular motors grip and then lock, holding tension at a small fraction of the usual energetic cost after the activating signal has faded]{claim=VASO-C010}. In the model, cross-bridges that have been switched off chemically — dephosphorylated — remain attached and detach only slowly, so a vessel can sustain high stress at low levels of activation. Arteries must hold tone for a lifetime; the latch is how they afford it. It is a kinetic trap, not damage — latched tissue looks normal under a microscope. And it is history-dependent: the tissue’s present state depends on what was done to it. A cheap, history-dependent hold that persists after its input fades is, in engineering terms, a memory element. Two questions follow. Is anything ever written to it? And does it exist in the vessels a knot would need?

Here the speed of the felt release becomes the crucial clue. Structural change in tissue — remodeling, scarring — takes days to weeks. [A change that completes in seconds, mid-exhale, must be a change of maintained state, not of structure]{claim=VASO-C011}: something the body is doing and can stop doing. Scar tissue does not release on an exhale. The inference is sound, and this case grades it as provisionally supported on physiological priors rather than on any record in its ledger — with two caveats. Its premise, that the felt release corresponds to an objective local event, is precisely the thing never measured. And “state” is a bigger tent than “vascular”: sustained motor guarding is a state; so is fascial densification — the proposal, from fascia researchers, that viscous hyaluronan between fascial layers thickens and then thins again under pressure, movement and warmth. If densification can reverse in seconds, the knot could be a state without being a latch. Nobody in this ledger has yet retrieved the timescale, which is why the research agenda asks for it.

## What the arteriole record actually says

This is where the case’s own study lands, and it lands against the comfortable assumption. A frozen-criteria evidence map (study VASO-S001) asked a narrow question: where, by vessel type and caliber, has the latch actually been demonstrated with a contemporaneous readout of activation or energetic cost? Sixteen eligible rows, 1981 to 2022, answered three ways.

First, the energetic argument — that a knot could be held for almost nothing — rests entirely on large conduit arteries. Every measurement of oxygen consumption, lactate release or ATP turnover during maintained force comes from swine or porcine carotid preparations held at zero transmural pressure. No arteriole or resistance microvessel of any bed has ever had its holding cost measured. Searches aimed specifically at arteriole energetics returned nothing.

Second, the compartment the hypothesis names has been examined, and what was found does not look like a latch. Three rows are pressurized rat skeletal-muscle arterioles — cremaster and gracilis, roughly a hundred micrometers across — in which myosin light-chain phosphorylation, the molecular marker of activation, was measured against diameter. In all three, maintained constriction came with maintained or *rising* phosphorylation: 27.7 percent at 30 mmHg rising to 39.6 percent at 120 mmHg in one study; about 40 percent at 10 mmHg rising to about 55 percent at 80 mmHg in another, attributed there to calcium sensitization and actin polymerization. A 2000 paper states flatly that arteriolar tone “represents a state of maintained smooth muscle activation that requires increases in [Ca2+]i and myosin light-chain phosphorylation.” That is the opposite signature to the economical, dephosphorylated hold a latch requires. The cautions are real: none of the three was designed as a latch test; all held their stimulus present throughout, and myogenic tone is by construction a response to a maintained stimulus, so they could not have seen input-free persistence even if it exists; and the rows were built from abstracts. But the assumption that the arteriole was simply unexamined is gone.

Third, latch behavior is not generic across vascular smooth muscle. The one published comparison between a vessel and its own downstream branch — rabbit femoral artery against its saphenous branch — found sustained stress at falling calcium in the parent (42 percent phosphorylation) and a forty-percent stress loss in the branch (28 percent), attributed to motor-protein isoforms that do not support latch-bridge formation. One laboratory, one pair of papers, and nobody has followed the comparison further downstream. Vessel type and motor-protein phenotype are load-bearing variables, not incidental ones.

So the mechanism the knot hypothesis borrows is real where it has been studied, and unobserved — arguably pointed away from — where the hypothesis needs it. That is not a refutation. It is a mismatch, and a specific gap the research agenda now targets.

## What if blood talks back?

In 2008 the neuroscientists Christopher Moore and Rosa Cao proposed the hemo-neural hypothesis: that coupling between neurons and blood runs both ways — that [local vascular and hemodynamic state can modulate what nearby neurons do]{claim=VASO-C012}, through mechanical, thermal and chemical channels. It was a hypothesis paper; it demonstrated nothing new. Sixteen years later, in 2024, Jammal Salameh and colleagues reported in *Science* that physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neuronal activity through mechanosensitive ion channels, in rat preparations and awake animals, on rapid timescales. The read path has a demonstrated mechanism. It is a mechanism of *instantaneous* modulation, in rat brain: it shows vessels can nudge neurons now, not that vessels can store anything and read it back later. Proponents argue that nothing in the logic is brain-specific and that peripheral sensory endings sit alongside the very vessels whose caliber they would sense. That extension is argument, not yet measurement.

## The synthesis, and what it would explain

The researcher Michael Edward Johnson has assembled these pieces into a program he calls vasocomputation, stated in three hypotheses of ascending ambition: that rhythmic vessel contraction acts as a compression sweep collapsing ambiguous neural patterns; that a vascular contraction freezes local neural patterns for its duration, functioning as a prediction and a medium-term memory; and that a contraction held long enough engages the latch and durably freezes nearby circuitry until the prediction resolves. Write, store, read: [vascular tension as a memory medium participating in mental life — with the grasping Buddhism calls tanha as its felt signature]{claim=VASO-C021}. The program is self-published, not peer-reviewed, and as of 2026 its experiments seek evidence rather than report it. The critical report commissioned for this case adds the sharpest objection: biological memory requires a state that depends on prior input, can later be read out, and discriminates between different prior inputs. A thermostat has hysteresis; it does not have an autobiography. The latch literature addresses none of these criteria, and the report notes that the nearest genuine write–store–read loop in a living flow network is a slime mold storing nutrient locations in the diameters of its own tubes — an organism very unlike us.

Whatever the fate of that grand identification, consider what the stack offers the humble knot. [A knot becomes a latched arteriole throttling its own neighborhood — chronic local ischemia at near-zero energetic cost, producing the acidic, sensitized milieu the microdialysis found, wrapped in secondary skeletal-muscle guarding]{claim=VASO-C020}. This would patch the oldest hole in trigger-point theory: the classic “energy crisis” model needed muscle fibers in permanent maximal contraction, a metabolic bonfire no one could account for, where a latch holds for almost nothing. It would explain why knots feel like autonomous objects, why they persist for years, why imaging keeps finding flow behaving as if something upstream were clenched. And it would explain the two-key protocol. Smooth muscle takes no voluntary commands, but it answers to autonomic state, and [slow breathing with extended exhalation reproducibly shifts autonomic balance toward the parasympathetic]{claim=VASO-C013} — a 2018 systematic review documents the rise in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia across studies of healthy people. Pressure perturbs the local loop; breath shifts the chemistry that governs unlatching. The roller is the read head; the exhale is the write head. Note, though, what the breathing evidence establishes: a global shift, measured on the heart, in people with no tender point in the study. The local, site-specific unlatching the hypothesis adds on top has never been measured.

## The conventional account, taken seriously

Every one of those explananda has a soberer candidate, and honesty requires displaying it at full strength. Tender points may be neuromuscular guarding: sustained low-level motor drive and endplate activity in skeletal muscle, centrally maintained and stress-sensitive — and the EMG chatter is, by every published interpretation, skeletal-muscle electrophysiology. The chemical milieu may come from compression under guarding rather than from a throttled arteriole. The felt release may be expectation and attention doing what they demonstrably do, riding the genuine but global parasympathetic shift of slow breathing, with pressure altering local sensation. Any rapid mechanical change may be fascial densification thinning rather than a vessel unlatching. And the construct itself has poor examiner reliability and no validated objective marker, so part of the observation base may be an artifact of training and expectation. This account needs no new physiology, which is its strength. Its gap is the set of localized objective findings — spontaneous electrical activity confined to a millimeter-scale nidus that a mental task selectively turns up, abnormal local chemistry and blood flow — that a purely central or interpretive story must still explain.

## The oldest anatomy text

{plate:IMG-VASO-P01}

Essentially every contemplative tradition that mapped the inner body arrived at the same three claims: there are knots, breath is the tool, and untying them changes consciousness. Tibetan tantric physiology describes channel-knots — rtsa mdud — constricting the flow of wind, untied by breath practice; Hindu yoga names the granthis; Chinese medicine records ashi points, tender spots named for the patient’s cry. The standard modern move is to file this as metaphor. The alternative reading is that [practitioners with extraordinarily trained interoception were producing first-person cartography of the vascular-autonomic tension system]{claim=VASO-C022} — channels as vasculature, winds as autonomic state, knots as latches. Proponents find it suggestive that the traditional maps cluster the important knots along the torso’s midline. But suggestive is all it is. This ledger holds no evidence record on the claim in either direction. Nobody has coded the traditional locations under blinded rules and tested the alignment against chance, and until someone does, every convergence is vulnerable to post-hoc matching — and even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches. The traditions also preserved a warning, which this case records without adopting a mechanism: releasing held material faster than the system can integrate is destabilizing.

## The crux, and what would change our mind

Strip everything away and the disagreement is narrower than either camp admits. Both sides accept the latch as physiology. Both accept that slow breathing shifts autonomic state globally. Both accept that people feel releases. The dispute funnels into one empirical question: when a knot “releases” on a slow exhale, does anything objective happen locally — a stiffness drop, a perfusion rise, time-locked to the breath, exceeding what pressure alone, expectation, and generalized relaxation produce?

What would move this case toward the featured hypothesis:

- Time-resolved imaging of a felt release showing stiffness falling and perfusion rising together within seconds of the exhale, at palpated sites but not sham sites, with the latch-specific ordering — blood first, stiffness second.
- A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after its stimulus is withdrawn, with falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost — the latch, in the vessel the knot needs.
- A retrieved primary study showing sympathetic blockade quiets the electrical nidus.
- In an animal, different induced vascular states producing reliably different later neural responses under identical stimulation, with oxygenation clamped.

What would move it toward the conventional account:

- Felt releases without reproducible local transitions, or equal transitions at sham sites and under pressure alone.
- Fascial densification reversing in seconds under pressure with no perfusion change — a fast, non-vascular state.
- A paired-caliber study finding the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles.
- A knot census finding that instrumented measures do not pick out the palpated spots.

## Where the ledger stands

The verdict is *unresolved*, and that is a finding rather than a shrug. The ladder is inverted: the best-evidenced rungs — the latch exists, slow breathing shifts the autonomic system, vessels can nudge neurons — are the least *diagnostic*, meaning they are exactly what conventional physiology predicts too and so decide nothing between the accounts. The rungs that would decide the case — that a release is objective, that the releasing element is vascular smooth muscle — are the ones with no evidence located, in either direction. The claim most exposed is the knot-as-latched-arteriole attribution, because the arteriole record now leans against it. The claim the whole case hangs from is the felt release, which is credible as an experience and worthless, on its own, as a mechanism.

The strongest argument for the hypothesis that this verdict does not answer is worth stating plainly. The classic energy-crisis account of trigger points has never explained how a fiber stays maximally contracted for years without exhausting itself; a latch would. The electrical nidus is millimeter-scale and stress-reactive while the surrounding muscle stays quiet, which is odd for diffuse guarding. Attention has now been shown to regulate a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site without arousal. And every arteriole study that found maintained activation kept its stimulus on, so none could have seen a state that persists after input stops — the very thing a knot would be. Finally, the hypothesis makes a timing prediction no rival makes — perfusion changes before stiffness — which is falsifiable and cheap. None of this is evidence that knots are latches. It is a reason the experiment is worth running.

## The research agenda

That experiment — ultrafast elastography and sensitive Doppler over a palpated knot, sites fixed in advance by blinded examiners, calibrated pressure through an instrumented probe, factorial controls, a button press at each felt release, and a mental-arithmetic block to catch stiffening during a purely cognitive event — would cost less than a mid-size grant and has never been run. It leads a program of nine items, ranked by how much each would decide. Behind it: a paired-caliber study following the latch from a feeding artery down through successive arteriole orders, with a stimulus-withdrawal phase, in the compartment the knot needs. Then two cheap desk items that sharpen the keystone: retrieving the densification literature to learn whether hyaluronan can thin in seconds, and locating the phentolamine study, if it exists. Then the census nobody has taken — there is no graph of knot burden against age, anywhere, for something millions of people can find in thirty seconds — with children and long-term meditators as the discriminating populations; a factorial trial separating the probe from the permission; the animal experiment separating vascular memory from vascular plumbing; the blinded coding of the contemplative maps; and the evidence map of the latch, already executed and reported above. A full-body ultrasound scanner announced in 2026 makes whole-body coverage imaginable, but it is a prototype built for body composition, not for the stiffness and flow channels a census needs, and it has no diagnostic clearance.

The machines exist. The practitioners exist. The experiments are small and specified. Someone should count. Either way, the knots are there. Press into one, and breathe out slowly.

assessment.synthesis: The ledger's ladder is inverted: the mechanism rung — latch physiology (VASO-E003), the slow-breathing autonomic shift (VASO-E009), vascular-to-neural mechanosensation in rat brain (VASO-E005) — is better evidenced than either the observations beneath it or the attributions above it, and every one of those mechanism records is credible without being diagnostic, because conventional physiology predicts each of them too. The anchor observation, a seconds-scale release of a tender point on an exhale (VASO-C004), is supported only by proponent testimony (VASO-E014): real evidence for a felt event, none for an objective one, which VASO-E016 records has never been imaged. Where the thesis needs the latch, the record points the other way: pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising myosin phosphorylation with constriction rather than an economical dephosphorylated hold (VASO-E020), no arteriole energetic measurement exists so the cheap-hold argument rests on conduit arteries (VASO-E019), and latch behaviour vanished one branch order downstream in the only paired vessel comparison (VASO-E021). The observational base is softened by the localization problem (VASO-E010, VASO-E011, VASO-E012), though the instrumented differences (VASO-E006, VASO-E007) and the stress-reactive millimeter-scale electrical nidus (VASO-E001, VASO-E002) survive it and are what the conventional account must still explain. The memory attribution (VASO-C021) fails the write–store–read test (VASO-E017); the contemplative attribution (VASO-C022) has no record at all. Sensitivity: no single removal flips the case verdict, because each direction lacks decisive evidence independently. The record whose removal would most change the shape of the case is VASO-E020 — without it VASO-C020 would revert from 'examined in its named compartment and mismatched' to merely 'untested', and the arteriole gap would look like neglect rather than a lean. VASO-E016 remains the single most important undermining record, but the verdict survives its removal because VASO-E019–E021 independently show the mechanism is extrapolated across vessel class and caliber rather than observed. Unresolved is a finding, not a default: the decisive experiment (VASO-R001) is specified, cheap and unrun, and both outcomes remain live.
assessment.steelman: The classic energy-crisis account of trigger points has never explained how a skeletal-muscle fiber could remain near-maximally contracted for years without exhausting itself, and the latch is the one known physiological device that holds tension for almost nothing — the puzzle the conventional account cannot dissolve is exactly the puzzle a latch would. The electrical nidus is confined to one to two millimeters and is selectively turned up by mental arithmetic while surrounding muscle stays quiet, which is awkward for a diffuse guarding story and natural for an addressable, autonomically maintained element. Voluntary attention has now been shown, in preregistered human experiments, to regulate a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site with no change in arousal — the write channel the synthesis needs, demonstrated. Every arteriole study reporting maintained activation held its stimulus present throughout, so none could have detected a state that persists after input stops, which is the only state a knot requires; and the latch-competent versus latch-incompetent motor-protein phenotype has never been surveyed in skeletal-muscle arterioles under chronic sympathetic drive, the condition the hypothesis posits. Finally, the hypothesis makes a distinctive, falsifiable timing prediction that neither guarding nor densification makes — perfusion rises before stiffness falls — and it can be tested for the cost of a small grant. None of this shows that knots are latches; it is the best reason the assessment cannot yet be closed against them.
assessment.whatIsClaimed: Muscle knots are maintained vascular-autonomic states rather than structural lesions: microvascular smooth muscle held in the latch-bridge state, throttling local blood flow and sensitizing local nerve endings, with secondary skeletal-muscle guarding layered on top — writable by stress, readable as stiffness and ache, releasable by sustained pressure combined with slow exhalation. More broadly, vascular tension functions as a memory element participating in mental life, the physical implementation of what contemplative traditions call clinging, and the traditional anatomies of knots and channels are first-person maps of the same system.
assessment.whereDisagreementLives: Not over whether people feel tender spots, and not over whether smooth muscle can latch — both are common ground. The crux is whether anything objective happens locally when a knot 'releases' on a slow exhale: does stiffness fall and perfusion rise within seconds, time-locked to the breath, beyond what pressure alone, expectation and generalized relaxation produce — and, if it does, is the releasing element vascular smooth muscle rather than skeletal-muscle guarding or fascial densification? Beneath that sits a second dispute: the latch has been demonstrated in large conduit arteries, and where pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles have been measured they show maintained activation, not a latch signature. And beneath that, the skeptical literature disputes whether the trigger point is reliably identifiable at all.
assessment.whatWouldSettleIt: A time-locked imaging experiment: ultrafast shear-wave elastography and sensitive microvascular Doppler over a palpated knot during breath-assisted release, with sites fixed in advance by blinded examiners, calibrated pressure through an instrumented probe, factorial controls (pressure with normal breathing, slow breathing without pressure, sham sites, failed attempts), a button press at each felt release, and a preregistered prediction that stiffness drops and perfusion rises together within seconds of the exhale, exceeding all controls, with perfusion leading stiffness. Felt releases without reproducible local transitions, or equal transitions at shams, would return the knot to the guarding-and-interpretation account. Companion studies decide the mechanism: a paired-caliber, pressurized arteriole preparation with a stimulus-withdrawal phase testing whether latch capacity persists into skeletal-muscle arterioles, and a retrieved densification timescale that tells the keystone experiment whether a stiffness drop without perfusion change is a live alternative.
assessment.bestConventionalExplanation: Tenderness and its relief need no vascular memory. Tender points are neuromuscular guarding — sustained low-level motor drive and endplate activity in skeletal muscle, centrally maintained and stress-sensitive — possibly with altered fascial gliding from hyaluronan densification between fascial layers. The acidic, mediator-rich milieu follows from compression under guarding as readily as from a throttled arteriole. The felt release is expectation and attention doing what they demonstrably do, riding the genuine but global parasympathetic shift of slow breathing, with pressure altering local sensation; any rapid mechanical change is densification thinning or guarding switching off, not a vessel unlatching. Nothing is stored locally: the brain stops guarding, regionally or globally, and interpretation supplies the rest. A stricter version adds that manual trigger-point identification has poor examiner reliability and no validated reference standard, so part of the observation base may be an artifact of training and expectation. This account requires no new physiology, and the only direct arteriole measurements available fit it better than they fit a latch. Its gap is the set of localized objective findings — spontaneous electrical activity confined to a millimeter-scale nidus that a mental task selectively raises, abnormal local chemistry and blood flow — that a purely central or interpretive story must still account for.

components.label: The phenomenon: tender points and their instrumented differences (C001, C005, C030)
components.note: Instrumented differences at trigger-point sites (acidic mediator-rich milieu, imaging-distinguishable stiffness and flow) survive systematic review with caveats, but manual localization is unreliable, no reference standard exists, and the mediator elevation was not purely local. The observation base is real but softer than it feels.

components.label: The neural signature: an electrically maintained, stress-reactive nidus (C002, C003)
components.note: One lineage, two small 1990s studies, never replicated with modern instrumentation, no vascular endpoint. What they show — a discrete site maintained by ongoing activity and dialed up by a purely mental task — is the strongest evidence for 'state' and neutral between vascular and neuromuscular accounts.

components.label: The autonomic lever: breath and attention reach the periphery (C013, C006)
components.note: Slow breathing's parasympathetic shift is well documented globally; voluntary attention has been shown to regulate a peripheral inflammatory response at a chosen site without arousal. Neither record touches a tender point or a seconds timescale.

components.label: The latch as physiology (C010)
components.note: Textbook smooth-muscle mechanism, but not generic across vascular smooth muscle: present in a parent artery and absent one branch order later in the only paired comparison, with motor-protein phenotype as the deciding variable.

components.label: The latch at the knot: state not scar, and vascular in particular (C020, C011, C004)
components.note: The felt release is testimony; no objective release has been imaged; no latch has been identified at a tender point; pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained activation rather than the latch signature; arteriole energetic cost has never been measured. Direct records lean against, but none was a latch test and none imaged a release.

components.label: Vasocomputation and the contemplative maps (C012, C021, C022)
components.note: The read path (vascular state modulating neurons) has a demonstrated mechanism in rat brain as instantaneous modulation; the memory attribution meets no write–store–read criterion and the contemplative-map attribution has no evidence record at all.

researchPriority.reason: The central crux is decidable by a single small-grant experiment that has never been run, both of whose outcomes would be decisive; two cheap desk items would sharpen its discriminating prediction; and the phenomenon is ubiquitous, clinically consequential and, on the ledger's own census finding, wholly uncounted.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only records are VASO-E013, the originator's own statement of the hypothesis (self-published, no experimental validation), and VASO-E017, which qualifies it: biological memory requires state dependent on prior input, later readable, and discriminating between prior inputs, and the latch literature addresses none of these. The claim depends on VASO-C010 (real capability, not generic) and VASO-C012 (instantaneous modulation demonstrated, storage not). No record shows content written to and read from vascular state in any mammal.

treatment.plainLanguage: The idea that the tension in your blood-vessel walls is part of how you think and hold expectations — that the felt grip of craving has a vascular address.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: No experiment separating vascular memory from vascular plumbing has been run; the claim currently cannot discriminate between accounts because nothing tests it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Hysteresis is not memory. A thermostat's state depends on its history, yet it stores no content; nothing in the latch literature shows different prior inputs producing different, later-readable vascular states.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A positive result in the decisive animal experiment (VASO-R005): different induced vascular states biasing later neural responses under identical stimulation with oxygenation and metabolism clamped.
A clean negative in the same design — vascular manipulation affecting neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion — would collapse the claim to ordinary neurovascular physiology.
Any peer-reviewed demonstration of write–store–read in a mammalian vascular bed.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No record supports the claim directly; VASO-E013 states it. VASO-E016 (strong) records that both linchpins — an objective seconds-scale release and a smooth-muscle latch at a trigger point — have no located evidence in either direction. VASO-E019 shows the cheap-hold argument rests on conduit arteries, never measured in any arteriole. VASO-E020 shows that in the pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles that have been measured, constriction is accompanied by maintained or rising phosphorylation — maintained activation, not a latch — though none was designed as a latch test and all held stimulus present. Indirect support from VASO-C002, VASO-C003 and VASO-C005 fits the guarding account equally. The direct record leans against; nothing is decisive.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a tiny artery clamped shut by its own muscle in a low-energy lock, starving its neighborhood and making the nerves there sore — not damaged or scarred tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis itself; establishing or excluding a latch at a tender point would decide the case between the vascular, guarding and densification accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: The compartment the claim names has been examined with the right molecular readout, and what was found there points to a different mechanism for holding constriction; meanwhile the release it must explain has never been shown to be objective.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A time-locked imaged release with perfusion rising before stiffness falls, at palpated but not sham sites (VASO-R001).
A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal with falling phosphorylation and low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
Felt releases without local transitions, or densification reversing in seconds with no perfusion change (VASO-R001, VASO-R008), would move the claim toward contradicted.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No evidence record in the ledger bears on this claim in either direction. The proposed alignment of traditional knot locations with vascular or autonomic anatomy has never been coded under blinded rules or tested against chance. The verdict rests on the absence of any test, not on a balance of evidence.

treatment.plainLanguage: That the Tibetan, Indian and Chinese maps of inner knots and channels are honest observational records of the same tension system, made by people trained to feel inside their own bodies.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine spatial alignment between traditional maps and vascular geography would not show that anything latches; the claim decides little about the mechanism.
treatment.strongestObjection: Post-hoc matching: with enough anatomical targets, any set of body points can be made to align with something, and no blinded coding has been attempted.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi-point locations into a common coordinate system that aligns with vascular branch points, sympathetic chains or dorsal root ganglia above chance (VASO-R006).
A blinded coding that fails to beat chance would retire the convergence argument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E003 (strong): Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces the observed high sustained stress at low myosin phosphorylation — economical force maintenance after activation subsides — in vascular and visceral smooth-muscle preparations, and is textbook physiology. VASO-E021 qualifies without contradicting: in the one paired vessel comparison, the femoral artery latched and its saphenous branch did not, so the capability is real but not generic across vascular smooth muscle. The claim states a capability and the capability is demonstrated.

treatment.plainLanguage: The muscle in artery walls can grip and then lock, holding tension cheaply long after the signal that told it to squeeze has faded.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Conventional physiology predicts the latch just as well as the featured hypothesis does; that the mechanism exists says nothing about whether it is engaged at a tender point.
treatment.strongestObjection: Latch behaviour depends on vessel type and motor-protein phenotype and disappeared one branch order downstream in the only comparison; extending it to resistance arterioles is an extrapolation.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A skeletal-muscle arteriole showing sustained constriction after stimulus withdrawal with falling phosphorylation would extend the claim's reach to the caliber the case needs.
A survey finding the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles would confine the capability to conduit vessels.

claimAssessments.reasoning: No evidence record is anchored to this claim; the verdict leans on physiological priors — structural remodeling takes days to weeks, so a change completing within seconds must be a change of maintained state. The inference is conditional and sound, but its antecedent (an objective seconds-scale release, VASO-C004) is unmeasured per VASO-E016, and its consequent distinguishes state from structure without distinguishing vascular from neuromuscular or fascial states.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really does change in a few seconds, then it was something the body was actively doing, not scar tissue — scar does not dissolve on an exhale.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Decisive against the 'scar' account if its premise is met; neutral among the state-level accounts (latch, guarding, densification).
treatment.strongestObjection: The premise is exactly what has never been measured, and 'state, not structure' is compatible with guarding switching off or fascial hyaluronan thinning, neither of which involves a vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Imaging that shows or fails to show an objective seconds-scale change at a felt release (VASO-R001).
A retrieved densification timescale showing seconds-scale reversal under pressure (VASO-R008), which would preserve the claim but sever its link to the vascular attribution.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E004 is a hypothesis paper (context only). VASO-E005 (strong) demonstrates that physiological blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neuronal activity via mechanosensitive ion channels in rat preparations and awake animals. The claim as stated — local vascular state can modulate nearby neurons — is demonstrated in one tissue, one species, as instantaneous mechanosensation, not as storage or content-specific readout and not in the human periphery.

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood does not just feed neurons; changes in the vessels can nudge what nearby neurons do.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for the vasocomputation read path but far from sufficient; modulation is not memory, and nothing here concerns tender points.
treatment.strongestObjection: Rat brain, instantaneous effects: the demonstration is of a fast mechanical nudge, not of a stored state read back later, and no peripheral analogue has been measured.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A peripheral demonstration that sensory neurons respond to local vessel caliber in a tissue relevant to tender points.
The decisive experiment (VASO-R005) showing vascular state carries a trace — or showing it acts only through instantaneous perfusion.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E009 (strong): a systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans finds reproducible increases in respiratory sinus arrhythmia and heart-rate variability and related autonomic changes consistent with a parasympathetic shift. The measurements are global cardiovascular indices; no local tissue or tender-point endpoint exists.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, with a long exhale, reliably tips the nervous system toward its rest-and-recover setting.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Common ground: the conventional account also predicts a global relaxation on slow breathing, so the record decides nothing about local unlatching.
treatment.strongestObjection: Everything measured is global and cardiac; the site-specific local effect the two-key protocol requires has never been recorded.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local stiffness or perfusion change at a tender point time-locked to the exhale and exceeding the global shift (VASO-R001).
A factorial trial showing breath adds nothing local beyond relaxation (VASO-R003) would leave the claim true and the protocol's breath component inert.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E011 (strong): a systematic review finds manual trigger-point examination not demonstrated reliable or valid, with no accepted reference standard. VASO-E010 (moderate): the principal peer-reviewed critique argues the construct rests on circular reasoning; it was answered by a rebuttal, so the construct is contested rather than refuted. Both records support the claim as written.

treatment.plainLanguage: Doctors and therapists pressing on the same muscle do not reliably agree where the trigger point is, there is no gold standard for what one is, and some researchers argue the whole idea is built on circular reasoning.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Weakens the observational base the featured hypothesis builds on, but only partly: the critique targets manual diagnosis and the classic taut-band construct, and instrumented localization may escape it.
treatment.strongestObjection: Imaging and microdialysis find measurable differences at sites clinicians identify, and the critique was answered point by point; unreliability of the hand is not absence of the thing.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A validated, instrumented reference standard with demonstrated inter-examiner reliability emerging from the census protocol (VASO-R002).
Replication failures of the imaging differences would strengthen the critique further.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Direct records are thin: VASO-E015 (weak, proponent essay, with second-hand statistics this ledger does not trust) supports; VASO-E012 (moderate) qualifies, recording that the reproducibility and ontological status of the discrete palpable spot are themselves disputed; VASO-E018 is context on census feasibility. The verdict leans on priors — the near-universal clinical and lay experience of tender spots — and on the instrumented findings under VASO-C005, which presuppose locatable sites. Well_supported would overstate what the ledger holds given VASO-E011 and VASO-E012.

treatment.plainLanguage: Almost everyone has small spots in their muscles that hurt sharply when pressed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The existence of tender points is common ground; every account predicts them, so the claim decides nothing about their nature.
treatment.strongestObjection: What is disputed is not tenderness but the discrete, reproducibly palpable spot — examiners disagree on location and no census has ever been taken.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A knot census with blinded palpation, pressure algometry and imaging at fixed sites (VASO-R002) converting anecdote to distribution data.
A census in which instrumented measures do not pick out palpated spots would push the claim toward the critics' reading.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E001 (moderate): needle EMG from trapezius trigger points and adjacent non-tender fibers found sustained spontaneous activity confined to a 1–2 mm nidus and none in non-tender sites. Single 1993 study, one laboratory, small; the signal's generator is contested (spindles vs endplate potentials); never replicated with modern instrumentation.

treatment.plainLanguage: Inside a knot, needle recordings pick up continuous electrical chatter in a spot a millimeter or two wide, while muscle a centimeter away is silent.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Favors 'maintained state' over 'scar', but is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology and so cannot distinguish a vascular latch from neuromuscular guarding.
treatment.strongestObjection: The recorded activity is neuromuscular by every published interpretation; it is the conventional account's own evidence as much as the featured hypothesis's.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with blinded, instrumented localization and simultaneous vascular endpoints.
A retrieved primary study showing sympathetic blockade quiets the nidus (VASO-R009) would strengthen autonomic maintenance without settling vascular versus neuromuscular.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E002 (moderate): in fourteen subjects, mental arithmetic increased EMG activity at trigger points while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, without generalized tensing. Same lineage as VASO-E001, so the two EMG studies constitute one line of evidence; no vascular endpoint; the essay's follow-up claims (relaxation training, phentolamine) have no located primary citation.

treatment.plainLanguage: Doing arithmetic in your head turned up the electrical activity inside a knot — and not in the muscle beside it.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The strongest evidence that cognition writes to a specific peripheral site — the 'write' step any storage account needs — but sympathetic drive to spindles or endplates explains it without any vascular storage.
treatment.strongestObjection: n=14, 1994, one lineage, no replication; the finding fits stress-driven neuromuscular activity at least as well as a vascular mechanism.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The stressor block of the keystone experiment (VASO-R001): local stiffening and perfusion drop during a purely cognitive task, reversed on breath-assisted release.
Failure to replicate the selective rise with modern instrumentation.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E014 (weak, supports): first-person and practitioner report from the hypothesis's proponent, in an essay whose text was AI-generated at the author's direction, that pressure locates a knot and a long exhale releases it within seconds. The claim as stated concerns a felt release, for which testimony is the relevant evidence type; it is uncontradicted and consistent with widespread practitioner lore, but it comes from one interested source and expectation and attention cannot be excluded from any first-person release report. VASO-E016 records that no objective correlate has ever been imaged, which bears on diagnosticity rather than on the felt claim itself.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press steadily into a knot and breathe out slowly, and within a few seconds it feels as if something lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: As a felt event the release is exactly what expectation and attention produce and decides nothing; its objective correlate, if it exists, would be highly diagnostic — which is why it is the crux.
treatment.strongestObjection: A felt release is the prototypical placebo-sensitive report, offered here by the hypothesis's own proponent and measured by no one.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked elastography and Doppler showing an objective local transition at the moment of felt release, exceeding pressure-only, breath-only and sham controls (VASO-R001).
A factorial trial showing breath adds nothing local beyond rolling (VASO-R003).
Felt releases with no reproducible local change would leave the claim true and strip it of mechanistic weight.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E006 (moderate): bradykinin, substance P and CGRP elevated in a more acidic milieu at active trigger points — in about nine volunteers, and, per the paper's own title, at sites remote from as well as near the points. VASO-E007 (moderate): a systematic review of 33 imaging studies finds biomechanical and blood-flow parameters can distinguish active and latent points from healthy tissue, with reproducibility caveats; this characterization is second-hand from the critical report.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where clinicians find an active trigger point, the tissue is measurably different — more acidic, richer in pain chemicals, stiffer, with abnormal blood flow.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Chronic local ischemia would produce this milieu, but so would compression under sustained guarding; the findings show something is there without saying what holds it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The mediator elevation was not purely local, the sample was tiny, and the imaging literature is heterogeneous in technique and definition.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Census-scale replication with imaging thresholds locked before validation (VASO-R002).
A perfusion signature specific to upstream constriction — or its absence — at palpated sites.

claimAssessments.reasoning: VASO-E008 (strong): preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers found attention toward a histamine skin prick produced ~1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving responses in ~90% of participants across two cohorts, with no difference in skin conductance, heart rate, skin temperature or anxiety and higher heart-rate variability under inward attention; lidocaine dissection showed sensory and top-down vagal contributions. Single laboratory, published 2026, acute model in healthy skin, molecular mediators not directly measured.

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an itchy, inflamed spot on your skin made the inflammation smaller and shorter — without making you calmer or more aroused overall.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that voluntary attention regulates peripheral physiology at a chosen site, but the demonstrated route is vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes in skin — not a seconds-scale smooth-muscle release at a tender point.
treatment.strongestObjection: Different tissue, different timescale, different mechanism: nothing here concerns trigger points, smooth muscle or latching, and the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate skin.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication in another laboratory.
Extension of the attention manipulation to stiffness and perfusion endpoints at tender points within the keystone rig.
